neighbours.label: relative pronoun (that/who/where) right after 'the same <noun>'
fire: It turned out to be the same mechanic that had botched our brakes the year before.
We stayed in the same village where my grandmother was born in 1931.
She was interviewed by the same reporter who had broken the original scandal.
Ironically, they hired the same contractor that built the leaking roof next door.
He sat at the same table where he had proposed to her decades earlier.
Officials blamed the same software that crashed the payroll system last spring.
The award went to the same coach who was fired by the club in 2019.
Sadly this is not the same recipe that my mother used for her holiday bread.
quiet: It turned out to be a different mechanic, one that had never seen our car before.
We stayed in a small village where my grandmother had once bought a goat.
She was interviewed by a reporter who had just moved from the sports desk.
Ironically, they hired a contractor that had excellent reviews from the neighbours.
He sat at a corner table where the light from the window was softest.
Officials blamed new software that had been installed without proper testing.
The award went to a young coach who had only taken over in 2019.
Sadly this is not quite the recipe my mother used for her holiday bread.
